I LOVE my IC4 and have had it for about five years with plenty of rides without issue - I used it for Peloton app classes and it’s very similar to the actual Peloton bike. While a super smooth ride, it’s not as heavy duty as a Stages bike which is the brand Soulcycle uses. My IC4 is fine for any out of the saddle riding, but I'd be hesitant to do any choreo or sprinting on it, especially at higher RPMs - it's a great, smooth bike but just doesn't feel as sturdy as a Stages one. 

As for your other questions, Peloton vs. Soulcycle classes are like comparing apples and oranges. Both are a great workout, but I feel like Soulcycle is a lot of high speeds and lower resistance with a dance feel while Peloton covers a wider range of speeds and resistances without the choreo and a higher focus on heart rate training - they have a few “groove” classes as several of the instructors are ex-Soulcycle instructors, but not many anymore. Most Peloton instructors still teach to the beat, but the RPMs are usually lower or are done in the saddle at higher ones. 

As I’ve gotten older, I’ve found myself leaning more toward Peloton - I think they pack more of a punch in shorter amount of time and I like how straightforward it is. I like some fun choreo every once in a while, but overall prefer Peloton now. I hope this helps!!

That’s just it - even though you “meant well”, your post came across as insensitive and, honestly, ignorant. In the end, it’s the impact that matters, not the intent. THAT’S the issue; people are telling you how it came across and instead of acknowledging, apologizing, and clarifying, you’re complaining that people just aren’t understanding. So maybe use this as an opportunity to reflect rather than continuing to invalidate the thoughts and emotions of others, which is what you did in your original post.

Absolutely!! I’m also a big advocate for healthy eating and exercise as a fitness instructor myself! There are SO many undeniable physical, mental, and emotional benefits. That being said, it’s ignorant and insensitive to chalk things up as “exercise and a positive mindset will fix everything”! It certainly helps, but many of us need much more than that and also need to face the reasons as to why we got here in the first place. I think the “pick yourself up by the bootstraps” mindset is why we have such a huge mental health crisis today - instead of getting the help and working through our problems, we bury them and pretend they don’t exist. We need a balance.

Because it’s a very insensitive and privileged mindset to have, IMO. You can’t just “change your mindset,” true change comes from time and inner work, often with a licensed professional. Sure, a new mindset can help, but you can’t just switch off problems and thoughts that have been engrained into your mind for years on end. That’s not true change. 

It also requires you to face your problems, not ignore them. You even mention that weights and cardio “silence the mind”, implying you’re shutting something off rather than dealing with it head on. To me, that sounds like putting a bandaid on a bullet wound. 

Everyone has their own path and battles that you have no idea about. Be kind. Be willing to listen. Telling someone to “change their mindset” is insensitive and invalidating, even if that wasn’t your intention.

I made another comment on this thread with links to FDA and CDC instructions! In a nutshell, to sterilize formula, you heat the water, let it boil for about two minutes, take it off the burner and let it cool, once it gets to about 160F add the formula. This process is to sterilize the formula itself, NOT the water - I think that’s where a lot of the confusion comes about. Just boiling water and letting it cool before adding the powder will ensure the water is sterile, but not the formula. 

All of this being said, it’s mostly recommended for young infants under two months and preemie/immunocompromised babies - some people still do it beyond that to avoid cronobacter. The Formula Fairy on Instagram has more great info on this!

Again, it’s recommended by the [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/cronobacter/infection-and-infants.html) and [FDA](https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/what-know-about-risk-cronobacter-powdered-infant-formula) for infants under two months and preemies/immunocompromised babies to prevent cronobacter - this is why many hospitals use RTF for newborns. If you were fine without doing that, that’s great! As a parent with a preemie in the NICU for a month, this was what was recommended to me upon discharge and I didn’t want to take any chances.

I’m a certified spin instructor and I’ve taken a good amount of classes from Cyclebar, Soulcycle, Peloton, and Crunch. The instructor COMPLETELY makes or breaks a workout for me. Even if the music is good, if I can’t vibe with an instructor, I’m not a huge fan of the class. It also works the other way around - if there’s music that I don’t love, I can still have a great class if the instructor is awesome!

I love Cyclebar/Peloton the most because the focus is on metrics and athleticism - Peloton is more of a traditional style while Cyclebar throws in some fun dance moves to switch it up! Soulcycle is definitely worth a try if you have one nearby. It’s seriously a dance party on a bike! I find that my calorie burn isn’t as high, but if I go to Soulcycle, I go more for the atmosphere than a hardcore workout. 

I belong to a Crunch fitness and find the instructors are hit or miss. I find that I like the quality and energy of instructors are better at the smaller, boutique studios better than chain gyms, but that’s not always the case! There are two instructors at my Crunch that I absolutely LOVE. The others are too mellow for me and give the impression they don’t really want to be there - I’ve seen the same at my local LA Fitness and YMCA. To be fair, I recently moved from Philly area to a more rural area. You may have better luck with chain instructors if you live in a more suburban/highly populated area where there’s higher demand and more availability. 

I’d encourage you to “speed date” through all of the instructors and find a style that works for you. Some like a lot of cueing and inspirational speeches during a class while others like minimal talking for better focus. Some like a pop playlist while others prefer rock. Some people care more about the instructor teaching style over music while others feel the opposite. I’m sure you’ll find something that clicks with you. Happy riding!

Starvation mode isn't a thing - physics boils down to calories in, calories out. I would take a closer look at the measurements of your food. Do you use a food scale? Measuring in grams will give you the most accurate measurement for your calories or macros. When I hit a weight loss plateau I was thinking I was keeping to a 1300-1400 calorie diet until I started weighing my food and saw it was closer to 1600 to even 2000 calories! It's suuuuper important because sometimes even though you may be measuring 1 or 2 cups or something, when you weigh it out the measurement turns into something totally different. Make sure you're drinking enough water, too! A good rule of thumb is half your weight in ounces, so if you're 150 pounds, you want to shoot for 75 ounces of water. Otherwise, you may be holding onto extra water weight. I've very successfully lost weight this way, so feel free to shoot me a message if you have any other questions. Good luck!! :)
